subject: Re: SLA amendment request — uptime threshold and monthly remedy plan
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@northbridge.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@northbridge.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA amendment request — uptime threshold and remedy proposal

Priya,

Thanks for the quick trial run last month. NorthBridge is preparing the procurement packet for a Q3 deployment and we need to align on one point before execs sign off: the uptime commitment in your standard SLA (we currently see 99.95% in the template).

Given our compliance posture and planned traffic patterns, our procurement team has asked whether Redwood will accept one of the following for our account:

- Option A: Reduce the uptime commitment to 99.90% in the contract and implement a fixed monthly remedy pool equal to 5% of our monthly invoice if availability falls below 99.90%.
- Option B: Keep 99.95% but narrow the monthly credit cap to 10% with per-incident credit calculation.

We recognize this is non-standard; the ask is driven by predictable budgeting in our SRE contract. Can you confirm which (if either) is feasible and whether you can provide the remedy calculation mechanics (how minutes map to credits) and maintenance carveouts?

If possible, please include an example calculation for a 60-minute outage across one region. We have a tentative procurement review next Tuesday and would like a short write-up.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
NorthBridge Solutions

Attachment: none

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@northbridge.com>
Cc: Anika Rao <anika.rao@northbridge.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — uptime threshold and remedy proposal

Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity and the example request. We can accommodate flexibility, but want to preserve predictable economics for other customers and keep operational guardrails. High-level thoughts:

- We can offer two contract tracks:
  1) Standard Commitment (our default): 99.95% uptime, per-incident credits with a monthly cap of 10% of invoice. Minor blips (<=10 minutes per incident) are excluded when they fall within our engineered failover window.
  2) Reduced-Commitment Plan (optional): 99.90% uptime in exchange for a larger, fixed monthly remedy pool (we typically propose 3% of monthly invoice) and a discounted list price. This is simpler for customers that prefer a predictable, single monthly adjustment rather than incident-level reconciliation.

- Example calculation (60-minute outage) — preliminary, rough numbers: say your monthly bill is $200k and a 60-minute outage is outside maintenance carveouts:
  * Under Standard Commitment (99.95%): credit = min( (outage_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * monthly_invoice * weighting, monthly_cap ). Using weighting factor 1.0 -> ~ (60 / 43200) * $200k ≈ $278.
  * Under Reduced-Commitment Plan: outage would draw from the fixed monthly pool (3% of $200k = $6,000). We prorate the pool by measured shortfalls across regions.

Notes / asks for your team: are you open to the Reduced-Commitment approach if we provide a 4–6% list price concession? If so, we can draft the precise monthly remedy matrix and carveouts. Marissa and Ben — looped to confirm legal/finance constraints; please flag anything that would block offering a fixed pool or the proposed discount.

I'll attach an initial redline template and a simple monthly matrix for you to review.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

Attachments: NB_SLA_Redline_v1.docx (redline), monthly-remedy-matrix.csv (example calculations)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — pricing/credit cap guidance

Priya / team —

Quick finance take: the fixed-pool option is OK only if we limit exposure. If we agree to a 3% pool with a 4–6% list concession, cap the customer's recoverable credit at 25% of any single month's invoice and limit cumulative credits in a rolling 3-month window to 50% of a single-month invoice. That prevents a catastrophic single-account drain while keeping the bucket useful.

Also prefer credits applied as account credit (invoice offset) rather than cash refunds to keep bookkeeping simpler.

Ben
Director, Revenue Ops

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA amendment request — legal redline notes

Team —

Attached are suggested legal edits to clarify definitions and avoid ambiguity:

- Define "availability" at the region-and-route level (avoid global aggregation for multi-region customers).
- Exclude scheduled maintenance (>=48 hours notice) and force majeure.
- Add an "availability tolerance" clause: incidents under 10 minutes are not credit-eligible unless they aggregate to >30 minutes across a calendar month.
- Convert remedy to "service credit" applied to the next invoice; remove cash-out language.
- Add separate latency SLO (p95 API response time) with a distinct narrow credit schedule — we recommend not tying latency credits to the availability pool.

I redlined the template and included a short example in NB_SLA_Redline_v1.docx. From a legal standpoint the finance caps Ben suggested look reasonable; we should confirm with compliance whether any customers require cash refunds.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: Reduced-Commitment Plan (99.90%) vs Standard (99.95%) — NorthBridge options

Daniel / Anika —

Thanks again for the discussion. Per your ask, we consolidated options into a short proposal. Please see the high-level summary below and the DocuSign link for the version of your choosing: https://docusign.com/placeholder/NB-SLA-2026

Option 1 — Standard Commitment (recommended default)
- Uptime: 99.95% monthly, measured per-region
- Remedy: per-incident service credits calculated pro rata by outage minutes; monthly cap 10% of invoice
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance >=48h notice excluded; incidents <10 minutes excluded unless aggregate >30m/month
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 450ms, separate credit schedule (see redline)

Option 2 — Reduced-Commitment Plan (your requested track)
- Uptime: 99.90% monthly, measured per-region
- Remedy: fixed monthly remedy pool = 3% of monthly invoice (applied as account credit); concurrency into pool prorated across regions and dates of shortfall
- Price: 5% list discount to standard pricing in return for the fixed pool
- Caps: single-month recoverable credit <= 25% of invoice; rolling 3-month cumulative cap <= 50% of a single-month invoice
- Maintenance carveouts and tolerance same as Option 1

Next steps: pick Option 1 or 2 and we will issue a final redline via DocuSign. If you prefer Option 2 but want a different pool percentage or cap, tell us your target and we can iterate.

If you want, I can set up a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the example math live.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Commercial, Redwood Inference

Priya —

Thanks — Option 2 looks like the right fit for NorthBridge provided we can close with a 5% list discount and the single-month cap at 20% (we're trying to keep long-tail credit exposure lower). We accept the proposed maintenance carveouts and the tolerance clause.

Please send the final redline with the cap adjusted to 20% and we'll sign via DocuSign. If you can include the 60-minute example calculation for traceability in the SOW appendix that would be helpful for our audit team.

Daniel Park

NorthBridge Solutions
